file_roles.evidence: The map was mutated while being streamed, 'activeTasksPerPartition.entrySet().stream().filter(...).forEach(e -> activeTasksPerPartition.remove(e.getKey()))'. The fix collects first and removes after, '.map(Map.Entry::getKey).collect(Collectors.toSet())' then 'toBeRemoved.forEach(activeTasksPerPartition::remove)'. The commit names the fault, 'fix ConcurrentModificationException in newly added Tasks container class'.

rationale: The pasted trace contains no frame from any non-test source file. Its three lines are 'Assert.fail(Assert.java:89)', 'IntegrationTestUtils.startApplicationAndWaitUntilRunning(IntegrationTestUtils.java:892)' and 'StoreQueryIntegrationTest.shouldQueryAllStalePartitionStores(StoreQueryIntegrationTest.java:270)', and the message only reports the outcome, 'Application did not reach a RUNNING state for all streams instances'. So the evidence places the failure in the test harness, and nothing in the report connects it to the gold file or shows how a thread dying reached that state.
notes: The role is clear from the diff alone, but the link between this defect and the reported flaky test rests entirely on the commit message; the report itself never mentions a ConcurrentModificationException. This is the strongest example so far of a report whose stack trace points only at test code, which the benchmark excludes from gold, so there is no path from the evidence to the answer.
